midWorkFindings.finding: A contract violation surfaced as a bare 500 with prose and no code, which is indistinguishable from the service breaking.
midWorkFindings.howItWasFound: the shape read across the queue against the FIRST canary revision (2026-09-17T22:40:46Z, g150-shape.mjs, revision plan-review-00027-luk): three engagements answered 200 and three answered 500 with {"error":"internal","message":...} -- prose and no code. Nothing in the response said which of the two things a reader was looking at, which is why the fix was made before the second canary went out (2026-09-17T22:43:51Z) and why the tag-URL verification of that second revision (2026-09-17T22:44:10Z, g150-tag-verify.mjs, artifact _inbox/2026-09-17_g150-reasoner-path-build_tag-url-verify.json) is the read that first shows the same three refusals carrying NAMED codes.
midWorkFindings.whyItIsAFinding: the design's own words are that a violation surfaces as a 500 with a named code, and the code is the part a reader can act on. The G-150 surface read that produced this dispatch had already found three of six demo engagements sitting unreadable because nobody could classify their 500s.
midWorkFindings.whatChanged: contractRefusal() in src/reasoner.mjs returns {error:'reasoner_contract', code, message} for a ReasonerContractError and null for anything else; server.mjs maps it and leaves every other fault with its own shape. Commit bca8839. Wrong-way test added at g150-reasoner.test.mjs:407 -- an error carrying the SAME code name but not being a ReasonerContractError must NOT be relabelled a refusal.
midWorkFindings.verifiedAfter: the post-shift read (2026-09-17T22:49:02Z) shows the three refusals carrying codes uncertain_not_machine_derived, absence_required and uncertain_requires_named_reviewer_and_reason, and the probe's own predicate FAILS on an unnamed 5xx.

midWorkFindings.finding: Three of the seven demo engagements CANNOT serve the path, and that is the product working, not a defect.
midWorkFindings.howItWasFound: a read-only SQL read of plan_review_findings for the refusing engagements, after the schema was read from information_schema.columns rather than assumed.
midWorkFindings.whatItIs: those rows were seeded before the reasoner contract existed: they carry Uncertain determinations with no named reviewer override and no written reason, and Unchecked determinations with no typed absence. The composed path refuses them rather than rendering a determination nothing supports.
midWorkFindings.whatDidNOTChange: no repair migration was written and no row was edited. A repair is a decision about what those engagements should say, and the honest options (re-seed from the current matrix, or annotate them as pre-contract rows) belong to the product owner, not to this lane. Recorded as a leave_behind with the refusal codes it produces.

midWorkFindings.finding: The design's fidelity claim was tracing to the WRONG COMMIT.
midWorkFindings.howItWasFound: after the refusal-code commit, check.mjs still printed 'every claim traced to commit 578ac3567156' while the branch head was bca8839 -- i.e. the artboards were being compared against source-state dumped from an earlier commit than the one that would ship.
midWorkFindings.whatChanged: source-state re-dumped at the shipped head (dump-source-state.mjs --repo <lane worktree> --ref bca8839), artboards regenerated, both directions re-run. Same counts; the PASS line now names bca8839's tree.
midWorkFindings.lesson: a design that says 'traced to commit X' is making a claim about a moment, and the dump must be re-taken after the last code commit or the claim silently ages.

midWorkFindings.finding: Eight defects in this lane's OWN instrument, found by running it in both directions rather than by reading it.
defects: plainText() read data attributes as if they were visible text, so a citation check fired on the attribute that carried the citation (false positive). Fixed by reconstructing the row's opening tag before text extraction.

the bare-dotted-identifier regex matched UDC sections written with dashes in source (false positive). Narrowed to the dot-separated forms the defect class actually used (14.02.005) and to model-code shapes (705.5).
KNOWN_SECTIONS held only UDC manifest sections, so model-code sections the product legitimately cites were reported as invented (false positive). Now built from the product's own composed output.

the paraphrase predicate accepted a modal that named neither a section nor a book title, which both over-caught and made the predicate's own vacuity invisible (false positive + vacuity). Now requires the identifier or the book title in the same sentence.

DECLARED did not say the Cycle board carries badges, so its badges were never read (false negative) -- the p319 'a control that cannot fire' class. Fixed by declaring badges for cycle and by rendering the tag attributes in c2Row.

violate.mjs planted in-row violations with a whole-file swap and could not find its anchors after unrelated HTML edits (3 PLANT FAILED cases, a harness defect that would have read as a passing suite). Replaced with an inRow() anchor scoped to the rule's own row.
check.mjs reported vacuity before violations, so an abort could mask a real finding (ordering defect). Violations now take precedence: a board that fails closed is reported as the violation it is.

one predicate path compared the artboard against ITSELF instead of against the product's output -- exactly the defect class the design is about, reproduced inside the check written to catch it. Every predicate now reports matched-input counts and compares rendered value to source-state value.
midWorkFindings.whyThisIsTheMostTransferableResult: the instrument was wrong in both directions (three false positives, one false negative, one vacuity, one harness non-event, one ordering error) and NONE of it was visible by reading the code. The self-tests inside check.mjs (72) and the both-directions run are what surfaced it.

gate2SecondAdjudicatorResult.question: Does the badge disappear for a rule once a second adjudicator exists, or is the badge a property of the drawing?
gate2SecondAdjudicatorResult.result: CONFIRMED, in-process and in the drawing. g150-reasoner.test.mjs:88 installs a second adjudicator fixture and asserts the badge for THAT rule disappears while the front-setback row keeps LIVE CHECK. violate.mjs plants the same shape on the real artboard (GATE 2 a second adjudicator changes the badge) and requires check.mjs to catch it; it does.
gate2SecondAdjudicatorResult.theOtherDirection: g150-reasoner.test.mjs:150 -- Pass and Fail are still genuinely reachable for the one adjudicated rule, so the fixture is not demonstrated by breaking the only real adjudicator.
gate2SecondAdjudicatorResult.theWrongWayThroughTheContract: violate.mjs 'GATE 2 the wrong way through the contract must throw for the stated reason' -- a machine Uncertain carrying the wrong code name is caught by name (uncertain_not_machine_derived), not merely caught.
